name: GigaSpaces XAP
tagline: GigaSpaces' Java in-memory data grid with space-based processing, SQL queries and tiered storage.
description: XAP is the in-memory data grid and application platform from GigaSpaces, a New York-headquartered company founded in 2000. It grew out of the JavaSpaces 'space-based architecture' model: data objects and the code that processes them are co-located in partitioned, replicated in-memory spaces, with event-driven processing units, transactions, SQL-style queries and a mirror service that persists changes to a backing database. Tiered storage lets cold data spill from RAM to SSD. XAP 6.0 introduced the name in 2007; the product is now the core of GigaSpaces' Smart DIH (digital integration hub) and of its Zaphira layer for AI-agent access to enterprise systems, and it is sold under commercial licences.

scale.notes: Partitioned spaces with backup partitions scale out across a cluster.

strengths: Co-locates business logic with partitioned data for very low latency
Space-based architecture with event-driven processing units built in
Write-behind mirror keeps a relational system of record in sync
Long track record in trading, payments and retail systems
weaknesses: Proprietary and sales-led; the former open-source edition is no longer maintained
Programming model (spaces, processing units) has a learning curve
Vendor focus has shifted to Smart DIH and AI products built on XAP
useCases: Digital integration hub in front of mainframe or legacy systems
notIdealFor: Small teams wanting a simple open-source cache
Durable primary storage without a backing database
